neighbours.label: The word-piece 'ark' after 'H' in Hark- surnames (Harkins, Harkness) and 'uk' after 'R' in Ruk- names (Rukmini); other k-pieces in surnames fire weakly or not at all
fire: The deed was witnessed by Samuel Harkins and his brother.
Aunt Rukmini taught the children to sing.
Our tour guide, Miss Harkness, knew every street.
The bakery belongs to old Mr. Harkins now.
A lecture by Dr. Rukmani opened the conference.
The trophy went to Julia Harkness this year.
Senator Harkin spoke for an hour about farms.
The grant was awarded to Peter Harkai last month.
quiet: The deed was witnessed by Samuel Hawkins and his brother.
Aunt Rosalind taught the children to sing.
Our tour guide, Miss Hartwell, knew every street.
The bakery belongs to old Mr. Hopkins now.
A lecture by Dr. Rahmani opened the conference.
The trophy went to Julia Larkin this year.
Senator Parker spoke for an hour about farms.
The grant was awarded to Peter Markham last month.

notes: Card: 'uk' x6, 'ark' x3, 'ks', 'ik' in surnames. Probes: Harkins 1.15, Harkness 1.10, Rukmini 0.89, Aksoy 0.31; Mukherjee 0.17, Erikson 0.14, Zukerman 0.13, Barkley 0.09, Larkin 0.01, Markham 0.01. The + pole takes 'ank'/'ink'/'k' pieces (Benkler, Sankar), so the neuron seems to split k-pieces of names by the preceding sound; this test covers only the Hark-/Ruk- cases.
